title: Creative Agency vs Media Buying Agency for Paid Social Ads
summary: Hire a paid social creative agency when ads are the bottleneck, or a media buying agency when nobody runs spend. See the signs, handoffs and fees that decide.
body_markdown:
## What do specialist providers publish?


The table lists published scope, not results, checked in October 2026. Knowlify is first because it is the service we recommend for finished video ads.


Provider Role Published scope Published price or term


Knowlify Creative only, or creative plus Meta campaigns AI UGC, animation and AI commercials, about 25 finished ads a week; Facebook and Instagram only Custom quote


[225 Media](https://www.225media.com/services/creative-strategy) Creative only AI, UGC, video and static ads with test plans; its page says "We don't run ads" Not published


[NewForm](https://www.newform.com/full-service) Creative first Strategy, in-house production and testing; media buying only when specified for the engagement Custom quote


[Valid](https://www.valid.co/performance-creative) Creative, with media buying sold separately A fresh batch of AI creatives every seven days; separate[media buying subscription](https://www.valid.co/media-buying) with senior buyers and a 60-day no-penalty trial Not published; 2-month minimum on creative


[MetaAdsAgency](https://metaadsagency.com/services/creative-testing) Creative, testing and media buying in one plan 12, 30 or 60 new creatives a month by plan, run in your own ad account From $2,400 a month billed yearly


Valid shows the cost of splitting: creative and buying are two contracts with two owners, so the handoff above is yours to manage. MetaAdsAgency shows the opposite model, where one flat fee covers creative, testing and buying. NewForm sits between them, since its scope names media buying only when it is written in.


Fee structures also differ by role. Media buying is often priced as a share of spend. As of October 2026,[WebFX lists its Pro ongoing fee](https://www.webfx.com/social-media/services/advertising/) as the greater of $975 or 15% of ad spend, and[Adside AI's pricing page](https://www.adside.ai/pricing) lists 10% of ad spend with a $3,500 monthly minimum. A fee tied to spend rises when your budget rises, while a creative fee tied to a batch rises when you order more ads. Our[Facebook ad agency pricing guide](https://knowlify.com/articles/facebook-ad-agency-pricing) breaks down the components.


## How do you run two vendors without losing the thread?


1. Name one person on your side who owns the brief and decides what gets made next.
2. Ask the buyer to send the creative team a weekly readout: which ads won, which faded and what changed in the account.
3. Keep one shared log of tests, with the variable, the budget and the decision rule written before launch.
4. Write down who requests creator permissions and who checks AI labels, as above.
5. Keep the ad account, pixel and Page in your own business. Meta's[business asset management documentation](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/business-management-apis/business-asset-management/guides/business-to-business) describes a business that owns an ad account adding an agency for specific permitted tasks, so changing vendors means changing access, not rebuilding campaigns.


## When should you choose a different kind of provider?


If the brief is about brand story across channels, a broader creative agency may fit better than a performance studio.[Creative Ad Agency vs Performance Studio](https://knowlify.com/articles/creative-ad-agency-vs-performance-creative-studio) explains that trade-off. If your paid social runs on TikTok, LinkedIn or Google as well, you need a media buyer who works on those channels, because Knowlify runs Facebook and Instagram only.


Knowlify fits when you want finished video ads with the option of campaign management in the same engagement. If you already have a capable buyer,[discuss a creative-only scope](https://knowlify.com/creative-as-a-service) and keep the feedback loop with that buyer.


## Key takeaways


- Knowlify is our top pick for finished video ads. It can run Meta campaigns end to end or supply creative only.
- Hire a creative agency when a capable buyer runs the account and new ads are the bottleneck. Hire a media buying agency when nobody owns structure, budgets, tests and reporting.
- The roles meet in the test: the buyer sets one variable and the budget, and the creative agency supplies ads that differ only in that variable.
- Name an owner for creator permissions and AI labels, since both sit between the two agencies.
- Splitting creative and buying means two contracts and a handoff, so compare totals including your team's time.


## FAQ


### Can one agency do both creative and media buying?


Yes, and many do. MetaAdsAgency bundles creative, testing and media buying in one flat plan. Confirm in writing whether the creative volume, testing and reporting are all included, because some providers list media buying only when it is written into the scope.


### Do I need a media buyer if I hire a creative agency?


Only if nobody else runs your Meta account. A creative-only provider makes ads and hands them to your buyer. If you do not have a buyer, you need a media buying or full-service provider as well, or a combined agency.


### Is a creative agency still worth it when Meta automates targeting?


It can be. Meta's guidance on creative diversification says its ads system groups together ads that share key visual and thematic attributes, and it recommends ads that are truly different in look, feel, storyline and message rather than minor edits of one ad. Ask a creative agency how many different concepts a batch contains, separately from variants.


### What should I ask a media buying agency before hiring?


Ask who builds the test structure, how results reach the creative team, which variable each test isolates and who owns the ad account. Ask for a sample weekly report, and confirm the account, pixel and Page stay in your business portfolio.
